land.text: 'most of the East (Egypt, Syria and Asia)': Egypt, Syria, Lebanon, Israel and Anatolia as the Roman Empire held them in 259

predecessors.note: Valerian had been captured by Shapur I in 260 (Macrianus Major page, undated) and Gallienus became sole emperor; the East was left without an emperor.

land.text: Syria, Phoenice and the Levant: Odaenathus 'sided with the Emperor and marched on Emesa'; his authority later 'extended from the Pontic coast in the north to Palestine in the south' (Odaenathus page)

successors.note: The palmyrene-empire dossier has the matching 261 gain (counterpart roman-empire); Egypt and Asia returned to Gallienus (the pages do not say how).

capitals.name: Antioch (Antakya)
capitals.note: Fulvius Macrianus 'took Antioch on the Orontes as his center and organized the resistance against Shapur I' (Odaenathus page). [Reviewer eu-04-x, 2026-10-19: added; the author's note said the pages name no seat before 261.]

capitals.name: Emesa (Homs)
capitals.note: 'In early 261, Fulvius Macrianus headed to Europe accompanied by Macrianus Minor, leaving Quietus and Balista in Emesa' (Odaenathus page); Quietus was besieged and killed there.

rulers.name: Macrianus Minor and Quietus
rulers.title: joint usurper emperors
rulers.note: Fulvius Macrianus 'declared his sons Quietus and Macrianus Minor as joint emperors in August 260'; Macrianus Major (infobox 'Reign 259 or 260 to 261') was killed with Macrianus Minor in the Balkans in spring 261; Quietus was killed at Emesa.

correction.text: 'most of the East (Egypt, Syria and Asia)': Egypt, Syria, Lebanon, Israel and Anatolia as the Roman Empire held them in 259

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'They quickly took over most of the East (Egypt, Syria and Asia) while Gallienus fought in the West' (Crisis of the Third Century page, c. 260-261 'in the East'). Neither the Crisis page nor the Macrianus page gives a boundary or an area; Cliopatria's Roman Empire 260 shape has 4.42 M km2 and its 261-269 shape 2.55 M km2 (West gone to the Gallic Empire and the East to the Palmyrene Empire row), so the eastern provinces are not separately shown for 260. Egypt is claimed by the Crisis page but not mentioned on the Odaenathus page.

region.text: 'most of the East (Egypt, Syria and Asia)': Egypt, Syria, Lebanon, Israel and Anatolia as the Roman Empire held them in 259

ledger.note: August 260: Macrianus's sons are declared emperors in the East. Fulvius Macrianus 'declared his sons Quietus and Macrianus Minor as joint emperors in August 260, in opposition to Valerian's son Gallienus'; the Crisis of the Third Century page: 'They quickly took over most of the East (Egypt, Syria and Asia) while Gallienus fought in the West'; the Macrianus page: Macrianus used Balista's support and the treasury to have his sons elevated (undated). The land is that page's, not the Odaenathus page's.

early 261: Macrianus and Macrianus Minor leave for Europe and Quietus stays at Emesa with Balista. 'In early 261, Fulvius Macrianus headed to Europe accompanied by Macrianus Minor, leaving Quietus and Balista in Emesa'; before this Macrianus 'took Antioch on the Orontes as his center'. [Reviewer eu-04-x, 2026-10-19: added.]

region.text: 'most of the East (Egypt, Syria and Asia)': Egypt, Syria, Lebanon, Israel and Anatolia as the Roman Empire held them in 259

ledger.note: 261: the usurpation collapses. 'In the spring of 261, Fulvius Macrianus arrived in the Balkans but was defeated and killed along with Macrianus Minor'; 'The Emesans killed Quietus as Odaenathus approached the city'; Balista 'was captured and executed by the King in autumn 261'. Odaenathus 'sided with the Emperor' (Gallienus) and later held Syria to Palestine (palmyrene-empire dossier). The Crisis page says Macrianus was defeated by Aureolus in Illyricum; the Odaenathus page names no victor and puts the defeat in the Balkans.

wars.name: Usurpation of Macrianus and Quietus

zones.text: 'most of the East (Egypt, Syria and Asia)': Egypt, Syria, Lebanon, Israel and Anatolia as the Roman Empire held them in 259

wars.outcome: Macrianus and Macrianus Minor marched to Europe in early 261 and were defeated and killed in the Balkans in spring 261; Quietus and Balista, left at Emesa, were taken by Odaenathus's approach: the Emesans killed Quietus and Balista was executed in autumn 261.
wars.note: Odaenathus is King of Palmyra, a Roman client who sided with Gallienus once 'it became clear that Gallienus would eventually win'.

certainty.note: The pages name regions only (Egypt, Syria, Asia); no frontier.

notes: A rebel state Cliopatria lacks, requested by the eu-04-b report ('Macrianus and Quietus (usurpers at Emesa)', 260-261). Three pages opened. They disagree on where Macrianus fell (Thrace on the Macrianus page, the Balkans on the Odaenathus page, Illyricum with Aureolus on the Crisis page) and on the end (spring 261 for Macrianus, 261 for Quietus; autumn 261 for Balista). The territory is the Crisis page's one sentence; the Odaenathus page lists no Egypt. The palmyrene-empire dossier (eu-04-b) opens with the matching 261 events. Wikidata id unknown. The slug follows slugify(name); the eu-04-b report suggested 'macrianus-quietus-usurpers'.
